correctness.rationale: For arbitrary \(n\), strict integer increase gives the two-sided odd recursion \(kS_m+1\le S_{2m+1}\le kS_{m+1}-1\). Induction with the binary-to-base-\(k\) map and its dyadic reflection yields exact universal pointwise bounds. Explicit positive sibling-splitting recursions realize both bounds simultaneously. Power superadditivity and induction give \(n^lpha/(k-1)\le L_k(n)\le n^lpha\); a differentiable dyadic-block bound gives \(n^lpha\le U_k(n)\le (k-1/(k-1))n^lpha\). Exact all-ones and just-above-dyadic indices prove optimal constants. The packaged checker tests 32,000 extremal-prefix cases and 54,300 exhaustive small-split comparisons, but the infinite proof is independent of these finite experiments.

value.rationale: The motivating source proves only nonsharp polynomial bounds for monotone Galileo sequences. This theorem identifies the *exact* pointwise feasible extrema for the entire positive integer family and computes the optimal global coefficients and distinct dyadic oscillations, including the nonmonotone \(k=3\) regime that admits no nondecreasing integer sequence. The binary digit and reflected-digit extremizers make the optimization reproducible without exhaustive search. These coefficients are natural order invariants, not arbitrary sampled cutoffs or a cosmetic recasting of Theorem 12.
